newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Left-wing parties again lead NZ govt in poll.
newsitem.headline: Left-wing parties again lead NZ govt in poll.

text.p: New Zealand's conservative National Party government held steady in an opinion poll on Sunday but left-wing parties again looked set to gain comfortably more seats in next month's general election.

National was unchanged on 35 percent in the TV1 opinion poll. Centre-left Labour was down three at 16 percent, while the left-wing Alliance gained three to 15 percent. The New Zealand First Party, promising to uphold the country's economic sovereignty, shed a point to 19 percent.
The October 12 election is New Zealand's first under proportional representation.
The poll would give New Zealand First 25 seats, Labour 21 and the Alliance 20 in a new 120-member parliament.
National would get 46, while its potential partner, the values-based Christian Coalition, would get eight seats on the basis of its 5.8 percent of the poll.

Another potential government supporter, the radical free-market ACT, polled only 4.3 percent -- short of the five percent threshold needed to enter parliament, unless one of its candidates can win in one of the 65 individual constituencies.
It remains unclear whether the three left-wing parties, divided over policies and personalities, would be able to forge a stable government.

The proportional system is virtually guaranteed to produce minority or coalition governments, creating more uncertainty than under the previous British-style first-past-the-post system. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746
